title: Temporal slice orchestrator for kernel coalescence and attention prewarm
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: tail latency remains elevated for mixed-length streams even after existing admission policies. We observe many small prefill windows that fail to amortize attention KV-cache warmups and kernel launch costs, leading to excess per-token overhead and jitter at p95/p99.

Goal: implement a temporal-slice orchestrator that groups incoming prefill requests into short time-sliced cohorts optimized for kernel coalescence and attention prewarm signals. The orchestrator should: (1) delay tiny prefills by micro-slices to align kernel shapes, (2) trigger speculative attention prewarm for cohorts predicted to extend into decode, and (3) adjust quota credit quickly to avoid deadline misses for high-priority requests. The outcome target is a 20-35% reduction in p99 latency for mixed short/long workloads with <5% throughput regression and no regression on critical SLA customers.

Scope: runtime admission module, lightweight cohort predictor (latency-budget heuristic), attention prewarm hook that touches KV cache with low-cost kernel path, telemetry for cohort formation and kernel-choice effectiveness, integration tests and e2e perf benchmarks. Not in scope: changes to model compilation or new kernels themselves (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Temporal-slice orchestrator implemented and enabled behind feature flag.
2) Benchmarks show p99 improvement >=20% on mixed demo workload (short chat + long completion) with throughput change within +/-5%.
3) Telemetry exposes cohort sizes, prewarm hits, kernel-coalescence ratio, and per-cohort latency distribution to console.
4) Graceful fallback path to existing admission controller if prewarm fails or memory pressure rises.
5) Documentation and runbook for toggling the feature and safety limits.
notes:
Design decisions: we favor short deterministic delays (micro-slices 2-12ms) over randomized batching to make latency budgets predictable for PLG customers. Attention prewarm avoids full KV population; it performs a lightweight forward pass using a wakeup kernel that marks likely KV pages. We add conservative memory accounting to prevent unexpected spikes during cohort prewarm.

Tradeoffs considered: larger time windows increase kernel coalescence but raise tail variance for small latency-sensitive requests. We tuned for a sweet spot in internal tests. We also considered model-size-aware windows (longer for very large models) but deferred complexity to follow-up.

Telemetry: new metrics prefix runtime.temporal_slice.* (cohort_count, avg_cohort_latency_ms, prewarm_hit_rate, kernel_coalesce_ratio). Add alert when prewarm_hit_rate drops >40% or memory transient >10% over baseline.
